study.question: Can unscored content keys rescue context-conditioned retrieval without changing its signed target-weighted values or learned capacity? Observed limitation: g0-r0049-block_retrieval_transfer click AUC0.6683505199248908 is below g0-r0049-uniform_transfer0.668457307890924 by0.0001067879660332, at380.44 versus363.39 wall seconds; the blocked counterparts are0.6678264533260458 and0.6678548720585206. Each has32192421 parameters. Retrieval improves some auxiliary metrics and history_gt64 AUC (+0.0001631498882127) but reduces history_1_16 AUC (-0.0005242925069315); these are exploratory single-seed observations, not significance or causal evidence. Source inspection shows existing keys are projected from signed target-score-weighted block values, whereas count division and RMS normalization do not undo negative scores or tanh saturation. Actual incidence of these effects is not measured. The incumbent remains0.668457307890924, above source bests0.660646940486458 and0.660163362657485 and DIN0.6555440824200336; this proposal reports no new performance.
study.hypothesis: A secondary content-addressing query should select blocks using their unscored masked mean rather than reuse a signed target-weighted contribution as its address. Keeping those signed contributions as VALUES preserves target relevance and count intensity while removing one redundant target weighting from the keys. Task-specific context queries and existing history-projection columns are reused. If this distinction is useful under the fixed recipe, content keys will beat scored keys and the stronger uniform reference at matched capacity and defensible measured cost. Auxiliary context transfer may interact with the changed address; cross the key replacement with its existing attached/blocked gate. A positive result supports only this implementation-level distinction: removing score signs, amplitudes, saturation and scorer-gradient dependence is a coordinated intervention, not separate proof of any one cause.

nearest_work.difference: Read archived v4 lines250-289. Inherit target-conditioned unnormalized local activation and count-weighted values, but retrieve ten compressed blocks downstream using task context. This does not reproduce the original DIN architecture or claim new attention.

Read pinned commit90bb99a60724e975ec565836266fd86dcad0039d lines129-274: feature-conditioned queries, and separate sequence key/value projections267-268. This motivates distinguishing unscored content keys from conditioned values; here keys and output history projection share existing columns, values retain DIN activation, and there is no added projection, learned fixed query, recent/earlier split or heterogeneous mixer. Benchmark code is primary evidence of that implementation, not verification of original-paper equivalence.

Cached section2.3 lines17-29 places feature-conditioned history queries and repeated query decoding in existing unified modeling families. This proposal isolates a local key-input replacement rather than claiming a new unified family.

Resolved original-paper provenance; full original text is unavailable through this authorized record. Use pinned benchmark implementation only and keep originality and original-method reproduction unverified.

inherited_components: Complete standalone g0-r0049-block_retrieval_transfer source as the implementation parent, including every learned module, native Dice state and frozen input boundary.
Ten temporal blocks, uniform/two-feedback strata, folded training-support population and pruned inference; action-aware signed target activation and count-weighted values.
Five masked match/order moments, target-match counts, task residual banks, rank16 signed product fusion, zero initialized interaction outputs and independently gated auxiliary adapter context.
Historical uniform-transfer/blocked controls replay the incumbent exactly in existing receipts; they remain external comparison rows rather than additional proposed runs.
study.proposed_difference: Add retrieval_key_source=content|scored. After inherited compression extract values.reshape(B,10,3,V)[:,:,0,:], the unscored uniform masked mean already computed by every train/eval branch. For content keys project this mean with the existing first V columns of each task history projection; for scored keys keep block_base/count exactly. Both then use the same tanh, RMS normalization, scaled dot product, occupied-block softmax and multiplier mass M. Unscored keys include only supplied historical item/action values; target action remains excluded. Use common unscored full-history content for auxiliary addressing, but keep each task original signed feedback-stratum values. In auxiliary training detach the content tensor before addressing, preserving all existing item/action/scorer ownership; the context gate acts on both query and fusion through adapter_context as before. Cross key source with block_aux_adapter_context_grad False|True, all cells fixing history_retrieval=context and product fusion. No new module, parameter, buffer, loss, normalization population, raw input, host setting or target-conditioned base path.
predictions: Primary predeclared comparison: content_keys_transfer minus scored_keys_transfer on full-population validation click AUC is positive; practical progress additionally requires beating uniform-transfer0.668457307890924. All four AUC/Logloss and auxiliary mean remain separately reported; auxiliary-only gains do not select the model.

Difference-in-differences [(content transfer - scored transfer) - (content blocked - scored blocked)] estimates interaction with broad auxiliary adapter-context transfer, within single fixed seed; a positive difference alone does not establish improved click quality.

At common nonzero interaction-output weights and fixed content/context, content-key ATTENTION is invariant to changing signed target-scorer contributions while scored-key attention can change. Retrieved VALUES and predictions remain target-dependent in BOTH cells. Content-key gradients bypass scorer activations in the address only; the signed value path remains attached for click.

At common weights, empty histories yield zero direct correction and one occupied block yields multiplier1 in both key cells. With multiple blocks, content-key gates can vary with context/content. Comparisons of trained empty or short-history slice metrics also reflect shared parameter training and cannot isolate direct retrieval.

No learned-capacity increase is expected:32192421 parameters in every cell. Estimate similar cost to r0049 (~373-380 seconds), but runtime, GPU seconds, memory and latency require host measurement; do not assert equal compute from equal parameters.
falsifiers: Content keys fail to exceed scored keys and uniform transfer in validation, or gain disappears under admissible paired repeats/cost comparison: useful retrieval rescue is unsupported for this implementation.
Any source-ownership, target-action, masking, shape, finite-gradient, checkpoint or scorer-replay parity failure invalidates the intended contrast and must be retained as a charged failed attempt.

No content/context sensitivity in multi-block gate checks at nonzero output weights, or gate dependence on score contributions in content mode at fixed content, contradicts the implemented addressing mechanism.

Benefit explained solely by changed gradient routing or auxiliary feedback partition aggregation would leave the specific sign-distortion explanation unproven; follow-up replacements are needed before stronger mechanism claims.
One-seed validation improvement after many adaptive rounds is preliminary; deterministic replay is not independent replication and no significance or novelty is claimed.
alternative_explanations: The previous retrieval deficit may be seed/optimization variation; its size is small and no paired user-cluster confidence interval is available.
Tying address and summary projection columns may be the actual bottleneck; changing their input does not remove that constraint.
Removing scorer factors changes key norms, signs, tanh saturation, gradient paths and auxiliary stratum mixture together. Content keys do not isolate those effects individually.
Softmax competition or M rescaling may harm short histories even with better addresses; the occupied-support policy remains unchanged.

Content addressing may discard useful target conditioning or magnify irrelevant/rare fields. Historical auxiliary labels are category/brand matched, and benchmark offline feedback maturity is not production validity.

Past positive product fusion contrasts are conditional evidence, not a universal transfer mechanism: target-triple0.6684064170805541, semantic-split0.6681449280610586 and interleaved-split0.668000056651913 failed to beat incumbent; target-additive0.667171929859184 was also negative. These trajectories remain in scope, not overwritten.

All evaluated trajectories reuse validation adaptively. Success against both frozen sources is not confirmation on a withheld population. DIN retains much stronger auxiliary AUCs than the click-selected incumbent; no all-task dominance claim.

knowledge_assessments.nearest_work_difference: Task-conditioned secondary compressed-block addressing with existing rank16 tied weights, not original DIN reproduction or a novelty claim.
knowledge_assessments.falsifier: Any changed original target-value path or masking/source-ownership violation defeats the intended adaptation.
